articles.headline: How Jalen Brunson became the undisputed king of New York

articles.headline: Jalen Brunson, Knicks keep focus ahead of NBA Finals Game 3
articles.description: If the day before Madison Square Garden's first NBA Finals game since June 25, 1999, was any indication, Monday's Game 3 between the Spurs and Knicks will be a madhouse. But Knicks players are doing their best to stay focused.

images.name: Mike Brown [600x600]
images.caption: An off day in the NBA Finals gave Knicks coach Mike Brown a chance to have a few laughs at a news conference attended by rappers Jadakiss and Fat Joe and actor Ben Stiller, among others.

images.name: Barkley: 'One of the greatest runs in playoff history' if Knicks win out
images.caption: Barkley: 'One of the greatest runs in playoff history' if Knicks win out

articles.headline: Spurs confident they can dig out of 2-0 hole in NBA Finals
articles.description: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs are remaining confident in their chances despite a 2-0 deficit in the NBA Finals with Game 3 set for Monday at Madison Square Garden.

images.name: Victor Wembanyama (June 7, 2026) [1296x729]
images.caption: Asked how he deals with the pressure of the Spurs facing two road games at Madison Square Garden with San Antonio down 0-2, Victor Wembanyama said: "This is what I'm built for."
images.credit: Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: What adjustments do the Spurs need to make to win Game 3?
images.caption: What adjustments do the Spurs need to make to win Game 3?

articles.headline: With Trump attending Game 3, watch party canceled, NYPD says
articles.description: As part of enhanced security measures with President Donald Trump attending Game 3 of the NBA Finals between the Knicks and Spurs on Monday night, there will be no watch party outside Madison Square Garden, the New York Police Department said Sunday.

articles.headline: Stacey King, 3-time NBA champion with Bulls, dies at 59
articles.description: Stacey King, a three-time NBA champion with the Chicago Bulls who became a fan favorite on their broadcast team after his playing career, has died at 59.

article.story: NEW ORLEANS -- — Zion Williamson scored 26 points, Dejounte Murray added 13 in his first game in nearly 13 months, and the New Orleans Pelicans beat the injury-depleted Golden State Warriors 113-109 on Tuesday night. Saddiq Bey scored 18 points, including a reverse layup he spun off the glass while being fouled to give New Orleans a 107-101 lead with 1:47 left. Former Warriors guard Jordan Poole added 12 points for New Orleans, which won its second straight and posted its fourth victory in six games. De’Anthony Melton scored a season-high 28 points for Golden State, but missed a free throw with 1:23 left and his team trailing by just four points. Moses Moody scored 24 for the Warriors, who've lost three of four while taking the court missing several key players. The Warriors played without Stephen Curry (right knee), Kristaps Porzingis (illness) and Al Horford (left toe). Curry, who has missed eight straight games, did not make the trip to New Orleans, coach Steve Kerr said. Only nine Warriors saw action in the game. Brandin Podzienski scored 16 points and Gui Santos had 15 for Golden State, which made just 24.4% of its 3s (11 of 45) but outrebounded New Orleans 59-53, scored 58 points in the paint and also had 24 second-chance points. Murry was making his return from a ruptured right Achilles tendon, an injury that occurred against Boston on Jan. 31, 2025. Murray played about 25 minutes, hitting a clutch driving layup with 1:04 left to make it 109-104. He also had three assists, two rebounds and steal, but committed five turnovers. Williamson's highlights included his first 3 of the season. He had attempted just three previously this season and made his only attempt from deep against the Warriors. He scored 10 of his points during the fourth quarter. Up next Warriors: Visit the Memphis Grizzlies on Wednesday night. Pelicans: Visit the Utah Jazz on Thursday night. ------ AP NBA: https://apnews.com/hub/NBA
